description: A modular, stack-agnostic toolkit for AI coding agents to autonomously find, reproduce, and patch vulnerabilities.

written.description: Reads a codebase and its commit history, builds a threat model from them, and sends agents to chase each hypothesis it raises. It then tries to reproduce each finding in a sandbox and attacks its own patch to check the fix holds, working from source alone with no running target.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(scan): a pull-request scan can write its findings as SARIF

The driver's report carries the gate's short view of each finding,
which has no description: a reader of the job's output sees a title,
a severity and a line, and not what the stages said is wrong. GitHub
code scanning reads SARIF natively, and core.sarif already writes it
with the paths made repository-relative and the message sanitized.

--output-sarif PATH writes the findings the gate counted, descriptions
included, after the verdict and the exit code are final.

- The findings are the gate's own: its open set, as it judged it, read
  back from the run's database by id for the description, keeping the
  gate's path (a rename's new one) and status. Archived notices are not
  verdict inputs and stay out. core.database counts 'reported' as
  suppressed while the gate counts it open, so write_sarif gains an
  include_suppressed passthrough (default unchanged) and the driver
  exports exactly what the gate counted.
- The title and description are model-written from the pull request.
  They go out through sanitize_markdown_text, the repository's
  sanitizer for SARIF (terminal control sequences stripped, credentials
  scrubbed, executable HTML tags entity-encoded), then core.sarif's own,
  into the plain-text message; no markdown field is written.
- A SARIF failure never changes the verdict or the exit code: it is
  recorded in the report under `sarif` and said on stdout, scrubbed.

Change-Id: I7754060969295850a4522102bc7a7e559f20c9e4
